explanation: Task-based programming (using `std::async`) embodies a significantly higher level of abstraction than thread-based programming (`std::thread`). The task-based model focuses the developer on defining the asynchronous work unit (the task) rather than managing the underlying execution machinery (the thread). This abstraction frees the developer from dealing with low-level details such as thread management, scheduling, and resource pooling, simplifying concurrent design.
practical_example: A team migrating a legacy system to use concurrency finds that managing thread pools and explicit joins/detachments with `std::thread` is error-prone. Switching to `std::async` allows them to define the tasks and let the C++ runtime environment handle the optimal allocation of resources.
keywords: std::async vs. std::thread, Task-based concurrency C++, higher abstraction concurrency
chapter: Item 35: Prefer task-based programming to thread-based programming.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
